claims.claim: The four workspace roles and their rights, including Admin-only Git connection and Viewer having ReadData but not ReadAll.

concept_html:
A workspace has four roles: Admin, Member, Contributor and Viewer. Each role includes the rights of the ones below it, with a few rights reserved for the top.

From Microsoft Learn's role table (checked September 2026):

Right Admin Member Contributor Viewer
Update or delete the workspace, add or remove admins yes
Connect the workspace to Git, create a workspace identity yes
Add members or lower roles, allow resharing yes yes
Create and change items, run notebooks and pipelines yes yes yes
Read lakehouse and warehouse data through Spark and OneLake APIs (ReadAll) yes yes yes
Read lakehouse and warehouse data with T-SQL (ReadData) yes yes yes yes

Two consequences surprise people coming from Databricks:

  • A Viewer can query a lakehouse through its SQL analytics endpoint, but cannot read the same tables from a Spark notebook or through OneLake APIs.
  • A Contributor can change and delete every item in the workspace, including production lakehouse tables. Contributor in production is powerful.

Rules that keep access manageable:

  • Assign roles to Microsoft Entra security groups, not to individuals (as in lesson A4-L2). People join and leave groups. Role assignments stay the same.
  • Least privilege per environment. Engineers are Contributors in dev. In production, deployment runs under an automation identity, and people are Viewers unless they are on call.
  • Keep at least two admins, as groups or named people, so a departure does not lock the workspace.
  • Workspace roles are coarse. For finer control inside an item, use item sharing, SQL permissions, or OneLake security (lesson C9-L2).

MIN_ROLE: dict[str, str] = {
    "connect_git": "Admin",
    "delete_workspace": "Admin",
    "add_members": "Member",
    "run_notebook": "Contributor",
    "spark_read": "Contributor",
    "tsql_read": "Viewer",
}


def min_role(action: str) -> str:
    """Lowest Fabric workspace role that allows an action.

    Raises:
        KeyError: For an action not in the table.
    """
    return MIN_ROLE[action]

title: Workspace roles, granted to groups
why_html: A contractor was added to a production workspace as Contributor "to look at a notebook". Two weeks later they ran a clean-up notebook against the wrong lakehouse and dropped three tables that reports depended on. Viewer would have let them read the notebook and query the data with T-SQL, and would not have let them change anything.
